name: CryptoPanic bearish spike faded inside an uptrend — buy news-panic dips in a bull (spot long)
rationale: MECHANISM (why bearish-vote panic within an uptrend leads a bounce): inside an established uptrend, a spike in CryptoPanic bearish votes marks a transient news-driven panic — weak hands flushing on a scary headline while the structural trend is intact. Such panics create dips that the trend absorbs; the vote spike leads the reversal because it tags the emotional low as it forms. The distinction from the RSI-paired capitulation spec is the CONFIRMATION: here a POSITIVE long-lookback ret_Nd (trend still up) is the guard that keeps us buying panics in bulls, not knives in bears. Exit when bearish votes subside (panic passed). DISCONFIRMER 1: if the trend filter alone (buy any dip in an uptrend) matches the deflated Sharpe, the bearish-vote spike adds nothing. DISCONFIRMER 2: if the 'panic' is the start of a real trend break, the long-lookback trend floor must keep us out — if the fit needs the trend floor set to always-true, the guard is inert. Requires CRYPTOPANIC_API_KEY; tier1, low-confidence until validated OOS.
catalyst: cryptopanic_bearish_votes spike (news panic) while the medium-term trend (ret_Nd over a long lookback) is still UP.
